q: 1. International Civil Aviation Organization (I.G.A.O.) was set up at Montreal (Canada), in ...........
explain: ICAO was established on April 4, 1947, following the ratification of the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention).

q: 2. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the speed of the aircraft relative to the ground, is called cruising speed
the speed of the aircraft relative to wind, is called air speed
when wind is blowing the direction of the flight, air speed is less than cruising speed
explain: Cruising speed is the efficient speed for long distances; air speed is relative to the air mass; and tailwinds make ground speed (cruising speed in this context) higher than airspeed.

q: 3. *The name of first plane landed on the old golf course which makes the present location of Tribhuvan International Airport is
explain: Historical records indicate early flights into the Gauchar golf course involved small gliders/aircraft.

q: 4. Which one is correct sequence with respect to the name of first airport in Nepal?
explain: The airport evolved from a golf course to Gauchar, then named after King Tribhuvan before gaining international status.

q: 5. *International civil aviation organization. (I.C.A.O.) was set up at Montreal
explain: ICAO was formally established on April 4, 1947, following the Chicago Convention.

q: 6. According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.), the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by ...........
explain: ICAO uses a code system (1-4) for length and letters (A-E) for wingspan/wheel span; textbooks often refer to the first five letters (A, B, C, D, E) for airport classification.

q: 7. According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.G.A.O.) the strength of runway pavements, have been coded by ...........
explain: ICAO pavement strength is often categorized by numbers in older technical manuals or specifically through the ACN-PCN numerical system.

q: 8. *The minimum length of runway for class ‘C’ type airport is
explain: ICAO classifications designate Class C runway lengths to fall within the 900m to 1500m range.

q: 9. The Maximum length and pavement strength of the runway is that of ...........
explain: In the ICAO coding system, 'A' represents the longest runway length and '1' represents the highest pavement strength category.

q: 10. *The minimum basic runway length of class ‘A’ type airport is
explain: Class A airports are designed for large aircraft requiring a minimum basic runway length of 2100m.

q: 11. *The minimum basic runway length of class ‘E’ type airport is
explain: Class E runways are for light aircraft and have a standard minimum length of 600m.

q: 12. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: air screw converts the energy given by the engine into speed
the propellers which are driven by turbine engines, are technically called turbo-props
the aircrafts which obtain the thrust directly from turbine engine, are called turbo-jets
the aircraft which is filled with a fan in front of turbo-jet engine, is called turbo-fan propelled aeroplane
explain: All listed statements correctly define the various types of aircraft propulsion systems.

q: 13. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1260 km ph. Its speed is known as ...........
explain: The speed of sound at 30°C is approx 1260 km/h ($340.3 m/s \times 3.6 \approx 1225$). Matching the exact speed of sound makes it 'sonic'.

q: 14. *According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.) the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by
explain: ICAO uses a numeric code (1-4) to categorize airports based on the runway's basic length.

options: sound varies 2.4 km p.h. per degree centigrade rise in temperature
sound at 0°C is called one mach
explain: These are standard approximations used in aeronautical engineering for the behavior of sound waves in air.

q: 16. *According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.). the strength of runway pavements, have been coded by
explain: Pavement strength is categorized using alphabetical codes (A-G) representing subgrade strength.

q: 17. The maximum length and pavement strength of the runway is that of
explain: Code 'A' signifies the longest runway length class, and '1' represents the highest pavement strength.

q: 18. *Runway is designed on the basis of
explain: Structural design of a runway pavement is primarily based on the expected wheel load of the design aircraft.

q: 19. Airport elevation is the reduced level above M.S.L. of ...........
options: highest point of the landing area
lowest point of the landing area
explain: The official elevation of an airport is defined by ICAO as the highest point of the landing area (runways).

q: 20. From the end of an instrumental runway, the approach surface rises outwards ...........
explain: For instrument runways, the approach surface slope is strictly regulated, usually starting at a 1:50 (2%) slope for the first section.

q: 21. *Stopping distance for aircraft during landing on runway should be,
explain: This formula relates velocity (V) and deceleration rate (d) to determine the necessary stopping distance.

q: 22. If the width of the approach area near the runway end is 150 m, the width of the approach area at a distance of 3 kilometers from runway end will be ...........
explain: The approach area flares out at a specific ratio. For a standard instrument runway, the width at 3km is calculated based on a 15% side flare.

q: 23. *Wing loading of an aircraft is
explain: Wing loading is defined as the total weight of the aircraft divided by the area of its wings.

q: 24. The strength of winds is measured with the help of ...........
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure that relates wind speed to observed conditions at sea or on land.

q: 25. If all aircraft is flying at a ground speed of 600 km p.h. in air having velocity of 100 km p.h. in the same direction. Compute the air speed of aircraft
explain: Air speed is calculated relative to the air mass; with a headwind, it is the sum of ground and wind speeds.

q: 26. The reduced levels of the ends A and B of a runway are 3025 m and 3035 m and that of its mid-point is 3015 m. The reduced level of the horizontal surface, is ...........
explain: The inner horizontal surface is typically fixed at a height (e.g., 45m) above the airport elevation ($3035 + 45 = 3080$, or $3030$ average $+ 45 = 3075$).

q: 27. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1234 km ph. Its speed is known as
explain: At 30°C, 1234 km/h is approximately the speed of sound, making the aircraft's speed 'sonic'.

q: 28. For class A Airport the difference of reduced levels of higher and lower edges of the conical surface is ...........
explain: For Class A airports, the conical surface extends to a height of 100m above the inner horizontal surface.

q: 29. Speed of
options: sound varies 2.4 km p.h. Per degree centigrade rise in temperature
sound at 0°C is called one Mach
an aircraft flying at 2975 km p.h. is called 2.5 mach
explain: All these points accurately describe the behavior of sound speed and Mach numbers in aviation.

q: 30. *Airport elevation is the reduced level above M.S.L. of
options: highest point of the landing area
lowest point of the landing area
explain: The airport elevation is defined as the highest point of the usable landing area.

q: 31. Effective length of a runway is the distance between ...........
options: point of intersection of the obstruction clearance line and the extended plane of the runway surface, and the other end of the runway
Point of intersection of the glide path and the extended plane of the runway surface and the other end of the runway
ends of the clear way on either side
explain: Effective length takes into account clear zones required to safely clear obstacles at either end.

q: 32. The lift off distance is the distance along the centre of the runway between the starting point and ...........
options: point where air craft becomes air borne
point where air craft attains a height of 10.7 m
explain: In airport design manuals, lift-off distance is technically measured to the point where the wheels leave the ground, but for safety calculations, it is often tied to runway length.

q: 33. If lift off distance of an craft is 2000 m, the clear way at the end of the runway should not be less than ...........
explain: Clearway length is generally calculated as 50% of the difference between 115% of the lift-off distance and the actual runway provided.

q: 34. The meterological condition which influences the size and location of an air port is ...........
explain: Atmospheric pressure and density (affected by temperature and elevation/RL) directly influence engine performance and lift, determining required runway length.

q: 35. The strength of winds is measured with the help of
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure that relates wind speed to observed conditions at sea or on land.

q: 36. The landing and takeoff of the air craft is made against the direction of wind. In no case the centre line of the runway should make an angle with the wind direction exceeding ...........
explain: A crosswind component is permissible, but ideally, the runway is oriented so that the 'crosswind' angle doesn't exceed 30 degrees for maximum usability.

q: 37. Beaufort scale measure velocity of wind at a height of
explain: Standard meteorological wind speed measurements are taken at a height of 10 meters above the ground.

q: 38. For class A airport, the difference of RL of higher and lower edges of the conical surface is
explain: For Class A airports, the conical surface extends to a vertical height of 100 meters above the inner horizontal surface.

q: 39. Pick up the correct abbreviation from the following
explain: All listed abbreviations are standard terminology used in aviation and navigation systems.

q: 40. The length of runway is increased per 300 m rise above M.S.I ...........
explain: ICAO recommends a 7% increase in runway length for every 300 meters (approx 1000 ft) of elevation above Mean Sea Level.

q: 41. The reduced level of the proposed site of an air port is 2500 m above M.S.L. If the recommended length by I.C.A.O. for the runway at sea level is 2500 m, the required length of the runway is ...........
explain: Correction for elevation: $2500 + (2500/300) \times 0.07 \times 2500 \approx 3958$. The key indicates 'b' (3725), likely using a different coefficient or rounding method.

q: 42. The length of a runway under standard atmospheric conditions is 1800 m. If the actual reduced level of the site is 1200 m, the design length of the runway is ...........
explain: Elevation correction: $1800 + (1200/300) \times 0.07 \times 1800 = 1800 + 504 = 2304 m$.

q: 43. Effective length of a runway is the distance between
options: the points of intersection of the obstruction line and the runway centre line
explain: Effective length accounts for the distance required to clear obstacles along the flight path according to safety slopes.

q: 44. For the proposed runway stated in Q. 47. if the aerodrome reference temperature is 17°C, the net designed length of the runway is ...........
explain: Following the elevation correction (2304m), a temperature correction is applied (1% per degree rise above standard site temperature).

q: 45. *The lift off distance along the centre of the runway is
options: at a point where aircraft becomes airbone
explain: ICAO defines this as the distance to reach a height of 10.7m (35 ft) above the takeoff surface.

q: 46. Slope of transitional surface at right angles to the centre line of the runway is kept
explain: For standard large airports, the transitional surface slope is 14.3% or 1 in 7.

q: 47. Meteorological condition which influences the size and location of an airport is
explain: Wind direction is the most critical meteorological factor for determining runway orientation (Wind Rose analysis).

q: 48. For the proposed airport, the survey project provides
explain: A comprehensive airport engineering project requires all these specialized plans for construction and operation.

q: 49. *According to I.C.A.O., recommended length of airport is decided on
explain: The basic runway length must be corrected for elevation, site temperature, and longitudinal gradient.

q: 50. The runway orientation is made so that landing and takeoff are ...........
explain: Landing and takeoff against the wind (headwind) reduces the ground speed required for lift/touchdown, shortening the required runway length and increasing safety.
